title: CROSS JOIN
description: Learn how to use the CROSS JOIN to combine every row from one table with every row from another table, creating a Cartesian product.

data.alt: SQL Server Cross Join StockTaking example

data.text: A CROSS JOIN allows you to combine rows from the first table with every row of the second table. In other words, it returns the Cartesian product of two tables.

data.title: CROSS JOIN Syntax
data.content: Combine every row of T1 with every row of T2 without a join condition.
data.code:
SELECT
    select_list
FROM
    T1
CROSS JOIN T2;

data.text: In this syntax, T1 and T2 are the tables that you want to perform a cross join. Unlike other join types such as INNER JOIN or LEFT JOIN, the CROSS JOIN does not require a join condition.
If T1 has n rows and T2 has m rows, the CROSS JOIN will create a result set with n x m rows. For example, if both tables have 1,000 rows, the CROSS JOIN will return 1,000,000 rows.

data.title: Performance Warning
data.text: Because a CROSS JOIN may create a very large number of rows in the result set, you should use it carefully to avoid performance issues.

Suppose the T1 table contains three rows (1, 2, 3) and the T2 table contains three rows (A, B, C). The CROSS JOIN combines each row from T1 with every row in T2, creating a new row for each combination. In this illustration, the CROSS JOIN creates a total of nine rows.

data.title: Product-Store Combinations
data.content: Return all combinations of products and stores.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_id,
    product_name,
    store_id,
    0 AS quantity
FROM
    production.products
CROSS JOIN sales.stores
ORDER BY
    product_name,
    store_id;

data.text: The result set can be used for the stocktaking procedure at the month-end or year-end closing.
CROSS JOIN for Finding Products with No Sales

data.title: Products with No Sales Using CROSS JOIN and LEFT JOIN
data.content: Use CROSS JOIN to create all product-store combinations, then LEFT JOIN to find which have no sales.
data.code:
SELECT
    s.store_id,
    p.product_id,
    ISNULL(sales, 0) sales
FROM
    sales.stores s
CROSS JOIN production.products p
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        s.store_id,
        p.product_id,
        SUM(quantity * i.list_price) sales
    FROM
        sales.orders o
    INNER JOIN sales.order_items i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
    INNER JOIN sales.stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
    INNER JOIN production.products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id
    GROUP BY
        s.store_id,
        p.product_id
) c ON c.store_id = s.store_id
AND c.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE
    sales IS NULL
ORDER BY
    product_id,
    store_id;

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: CROSS JOIN returns the Cartesian product of two tables (every row from T1 with every row from T2).
CROSS JOIN does not require a join condition.
If T1 has n rows and T2 has m rows, CROSS JOIN returns n x m rows.
Use CROSS JOIN carefully to avoid performance issues with large tables.
CROSS JOIN is useful for generating all combinations, such as product-store pairs.
